Contacting Sales at Canva

When a company wants Canva for its whole team, its first step is the Contact Sales form. In B2B, this is where interest turns into pipeline. The best submissions become marketing qualified leads (MQLs) for the sales team. My goal was to make getting in touch easier for genuine buyers, without letting lead quality slip.

Product Design
Role
Product Designer
Team
Marketing Technology
Timeline
1 Month
Tools
Figma, Cursor
Business model
SaaS/Tech

The Challenge

This form is the last step before a buyer talks to Sales, and too many were giving up. The fix had to balance two goals that often pull against each other in B2B: an easier form, and high-quality leads.

  • Losing buyers at peak intent

    These visitors are close to buying, yet only around 4% of pageviews became a submission.

  • Friction before value

    All 11 fields appeared at once, and on smaller screens the submit button was hidden below the fold.

  • Asking for what we already knew

    Logged-in users had to retype details Canva already had.

  • Volume that wasn't pipeline

    Personal email addresses were reaching Sales, adding noise and slowing follow-up on real opportunities.

The Solution

  • I split the form into two short steps, with the easy questions first.

  • Step 1

    Name, company email and enquiry type, which is what Sales needs to route a lead. Logged-in users get their name and email prefilled, so they only answer one question.

  • Step 2

    Company details, role, an optional phone number and “How can we help?”

  • I also changed the email helper text to “Enter your company email” to nudge people towards work addresses.

Design decisions and impact

  • Putting the hardest question last

    “How can we help?” takes the most thought, so it moved to Step 2, once people have already started. More people finish, and Sales still gets the context it needs.

  • Prefilled, but editable

    A Canva login isn’t always someone’s work identity, so every prefilled field can be changed. People save time, and lead data stays accurate.

  • Protecting lead quality

    We tracked submission-to-MQL and MQL-to-opportunity rates, work email usage, step drop-off and mobile completion. That way, more submissions wouldn’t come at the cost of pipeline quality.

Hypothesis

If we split the form into two shorter steps and prefill known fields, more buyers will submit it, because there's less effort and less repetition, while MQL quality holds.

Success criteria

A 3 to 5% increase in conversion or submissions, with no drop in submission-to-MQL or MQL-to-opportunity rates. I worked with Data Science on the test plan, and the form was translated into 31 locales.

The Outcome

We A/B tested the two-step form against the original, and it delivered a statistically significant +6.3% increase in Contact Sales submissions. It’s now live for 100% of users.

That means more buyers are reaching Sales from the same traffic, through a form that asks for less up front.
